title: observability: token & KV-level cost/latency dashboards, enhanced logging, and alert tuning
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Problem: teams need fine-grained visibility into per-request token costs and KV-cache behavior to diagnose regressions and optimize serving economics. Existing dashboards surface aggregate QPS and tail latency but do not correlate token-level cost with cache hit rate and sequence-length distributions. Alerts were firing too frequently for SLO-adjacent noise and lacked context (e.g., whether cost increase was due to longer prompts or KV-cache misses).

This PR introduces: 1) Token-level cost and latency metrics (per-model, per-route, per-tenant) including distribution histograms and p50/p95/p99 breakdowns; 2) KV-cache metrics (hit/miss rates, miss latency, memory pressure signals) correlated with token flows; 3) Enriched logs and trace spans to include token counts, sequence-length bucketing, and KV-cache keys touched; 4) New Grafana dashboards that combine cost, latency, and KV-cache indicators for fast RCA; 5) Alert tuning to reduce alert noise and provide actionable triggers (e.g., sustained token-cost-per-request increase with accompanying cache-miss spike).

Implementation notes: - Metrics: added Prometheus metrics rwi_token_cost_total, rwi_token_latency_seconds_bucket (HDR histograms), rwi_kv_cache_hits_total, rwi_kv_cache_misses_total, rwi_kv_miss_latency_seconds; labels: model, route, tenant_id (tenant_id is redacted for hosted customers unless org-level opt-in). - Tracing: added attributes to serving spans: token.count, prompt.length_bucket, kv.cache_hit (boolean), kv.miss_reason (enum). - Logging: structured JSON logs include token_count and kv_cache_stats when debug/trace is enabled; default log volume unchanged. - Dashboards: new dashboard jsons under observability/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.json (two panels: cost vs token distribution, cost with KV miss overlays) and observability/dashboards/token_kv_rca.json (correlation panels). - Alerts: replaced a single global high-cost alert with a set of contextual rules: HighTokenCostPerRequest (requires 30m sustained with p95 > threshold AND kv_miss_rate increase > 20%), TokenCostSpike (short-term 5m spike but only pages on customer-impacting routes), KVCacheDegradation (memory pressure + miss-rate).

Backward compatibility and privacy: telemetry labels follow current rules; tenant_id is present only for internal clusters and in dedicated/private deployments where allowed. No breaking API changes.

Testing: included unit tests for metric write paths and tagging, integration test that simulates KV-cache miss storm and asserts alerts fire only for scoped conditions, end-to-end smoke against a staging Grafana using exported dashboard JSON. Load test: ran perf-canary with synthetic traffic to ensure metric collection overhead is <2% p99 latency.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag `obs.token_kv_enhanced` - Enable for internal infra and a small set of enterprise tenants for 2 weeks - Monitor dashboards; iterate on thresholds - Gradual ramp to all hosted customers and dedicated clusters.

Checklist:
- [x] Metrics instrumentation added and unit-tested
- [x] Tracing attributes added and verified via sample traces
- [x] Dashboards added and reviewed with SRE/Observability
- [x] Alerts tuned, documented, and added to runbook
- [x] Performance regression testing completed

Files of interest are summarized below. For details, see changed_files and commits.
